extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: A fully authentic visual question answering dataset sourced from online question answering communities, where each example includes a natural language question, image, context, and an accepted answer validated by the individual asking the question.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, and Danna Gurari
extraction.citeAs: Chen, Chongyan, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, and Danna Gurari. Fully Authentic Visual Question Answering Dataset from Online Communities. arXiv:2311.15562v4 [cs.CV], 17 Jul 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by scraping publicly available Stack Exchange data and collecting examples with a question, context, image, and at least one answer; only examples with an accepted answer were used, followed by filtering for quality and format constraints.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Examples were removed when the image could not be downloaded from the provided link.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public Stack Exchange archive data in XML format, including post title, body text, image URL, answers, accepted answer status, and topic-specific sites.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: They filtered out low-quality examples with non-positive question or answer scores, excluded questions with multiple images or visual answers, removed examples whose images could not be downloaded, and converted all images to PNG format.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For user intention annotations, three Amazon Mechanical Turk crowdworkers labeled one primary intent per visual question using provided instructions, taxonomy definitions, and examples; two independent annotations were collected per item and a third worker broke ties. For human evaluation, ten domain experts rated model-generated answers as incorrect, partially correct, or correct.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For user intention taxonomy development, two author-annotators iteratively refined categories over four rounds, resolving disagreements and improving agreement metrics; for final user intention labels, majority vote from three crowdsourced labels was used.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For crowdworkers, workers were located in the United States, had completed more than 500 HITs, and had over a 95% approval rating. For human evaluation, annotators were domain experts in one of ten topics and each had at least a Master's degree in a related field.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors note the dataset may underrepresent people in poverty-stricken areas and has unbalanced geographic representation, with more users from the US, India, and Europe and fewer from countries like Egypt.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas and has geographically unbalanced representation, with more data from the US, India, and Europe and less from countries like Egypt.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas because it is limited to Stack Exchange users with internet and mobile device access, and its geographic representation is unbalanced.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset supports few-shot learning and is used for benchmarking VQA models with training, validation, and test splits.

name.evidence: We address these limitations by introducing a new dataset called VQAonline.

description.evidence: Sourced from online question answering communities, it is the the first VQA dataset with all contents originating from an authentic use case.

url.evidence: We publicly-share the dataset at: https://vqaonline.github.io/.

license.evidence: We used the publicly-available data that spanned from August 2010 to November 2022, and adhered to all data license restrictions (cc-by-sa 4.0) set forth by Stack Exchange.

creator.evidence: Chongyan Chen1, Mengchen Liu2, Noel Codella2, Yunsheng Li2, Lu Yuan2, and Danna Gurari1,3

isLiveDataset.evidence: We used the publicly-available data that spanned from August 2010 to November 2022

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We created our dataset by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We created our dataset by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: Finally, after removing examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided link, we got to our final dataset of 64,696 visual questions.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The Stack Exchange data is hosted at https://archive.org/details/stackexchange in XML format.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: We used the publicly-available data that spanned from August 2010 to November 2022

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: First, we removed low-quality VQAs based on Stack Exchange’s feature that enables users to up-vote or down-vote each post (either question or answer).

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We hired three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk to perform our task.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We hired three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk to perform our task.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We then finalized the taxonomy with definitions via four rounds of annotator analysis on a total of 105 visual questions.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: To enable the assessment of high-quality results, we collected two user intention annotations from two independent workers (worker A and B) per VQA instance

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: For quality control, we only accepted workers located in the United States who had completed more than 500 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) with over a 95% approval rating.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: To do so, we solicited help from GPT-3.5 by having it indicate via a zero-shot prompt the user intentions when given a question and context.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Despite the VQAonline dataset’s inclusion of multilingual VQAs and coverage of users’ generated visual questions from various countries, we highlight that this dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Intemet.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Additionally, the geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more from countries like US, India, Europe and less from countries like Egypt.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: we highlight that this dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and Intemet.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: VQAonline supports few-shot leaming by containing training, validation, and test splits of 665, 285, and 63,746 examples respectively.
